title: Mirabel and the Scholarship
premise: Tamsin Marchetti has spent years being invisible—cooking, cleaning, and covering for his night-shift mother while the town of Harrow's Bend celebrates its beloved Founders' Scholarship, which sends one lucky senior away every year. When his best friend Dev vanishes leaving only a ring of old brass keys, Tamsin discovers the Scholarship is a covenant: the town's prosperity is bought with the memory of whoever wins it, erased from every mind but their own. Dev won—and chose to run rather than forget. To save him and end the tradition, Tamsin must use Dev's keys to reach the Founders' vault beneath the school before graduation night seals a new winner, sacrificing his own chance at escape and nearly his own memories to break the bargain. In the end the town grieves what it was built on, Dev comes home half-remembered, and Tamsin finally lets himself be seen.
about_author: Ivo Coldharbour grew up in a fading mill town where every family had a story they agreed not to tell, and never quite stopped listening for them. He writes young adult fiction about kids who hold households together and the secrets that try to hold them back.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A morning in the Marchetti house: burnt toast, missing lunch money, three younger siblings managed like a small navy, mom asleep after her shift. At school, everyone buzzes about the Founders' Scholarship assembly while Tamsin keeps his head down. Beat: competence as armor—he's fine, he insists, even as cracks show.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Dev misses their standing Friday hangout; then his mother calls, frantic—Dev never came home. On Dev's porch sits his backpack and a ring of seven tarnished brass keys with no labels. Police shrug; a seventeen-year-old runaway isn't news. Beat: dread blooming under denial—Dev wouldn't leave without telling him.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin POV with interstitials of town archive clippings. Asking around, Tamsin finds eerie gaps: adults can't name last year's scholarship winner, photos are smudged, yearbook pages cut out. The librarian, Mrs. Okafor, goes pale when she sees the keys and tells him to put them back. Beat: the first real fear—the town itself is complicit.

chapters.title: Seven Locks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He matches each key to doors around town: the church basement, the mill office, the school's sub-basement. Each unlocked room holds tokens of past winners—a jacket, a diary, a hospital bracelet—all belonging to people no one remembers. Beat: grief and vertigo; the Scholarship doesn't send kids away, it deletes them.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with flashback chapters from Dev's journal found in the mill office. A 1987 winner, Ruth Calloway, surfaces in a nursing home outside town—alive, forgotten by everyone, including herself until Tamsin shows her the keys. She remembers fragments: the vault, the choosing, the forgetting. Beat: hope with a deadline—Ruth's memory is failing faster than Tamsin can harvest it.

chapters.title: Nomination Night
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The school announces this year's shortlist—Tamsin's little sister Priya is on it, and so is he, nominated by teachers who 'see potential.' The Founders' Committee, led by charming Mayor Whitlock, takes sudden warm interest in the Marchetti family. Beat: temptation sharpened into threat—the trap offers everything his family needs.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price Tag
chapters.summary: Priya's POV for the first time. She knows Tamsin is investigating; she also knows the Scholarship money would let Mom quit nights. Siblings clash: Priya accuses Tamsin of wanting to stay small forever; he accuses her of volunteering to disappear. Mom, exhausted, admits she's always known something was wrong with the winners. Beat: the theme made domestic—survival versus truth inside one kitchen.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the School
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with Ruth along as guide. Using the final key, they descend beneath the gymnasium to the Founders' vault: a ledger of names, a mechanism of mirrors and chalk sigils, and evidence Dev passed through days ago, leaving messages scratched into the wall. They're discovered; Ruth creates a diversion and is taken. Beat: point of no return—Tamsin is now hunted by the whole civic machinery.

chapters.title: Graduation Night
chapters.summary: Climax, Tamsin's POV. During the ceremony, the Committee prepares to choose Priya. Tamsin breaks into the vault's heart, finds Dev hiding in the mill tunnels above, and forces the choice the Founders dread: someone must take the forgetting willingly to unbind it. Tamsin begins erasing himself—his name, his family—while Dev and Ruth's recovered testimony broadcasts over the ceremony speakers. Beat: sacrifice at full cost, loyalty and truth finally aligned.

chapters.title: Tamsin Marchetti, Remembered
chapters.summary: Resolution, shifting between Priya's and Dev's POVs. The covenant broken, the town wakes to its stolen history—mourning, lawsuits, and hard reckonings. Tamsin's memories return in pieces because Dev held onto them, having written Tamsin's life in a notebook during the blank weeks. The Marchettis are poor still, but seen now. Final beat: invisibility was never safety; being known is the real survival.
